channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Orders Swift Resolution to Lawyer Shortage in Districts
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov criticized the lack of legal aid specialists in Kyrgyzstan's districts, ordering an immediate solution. He urged legal bodies to propose legislative changes if needed. The issue was highlighted by a resident of Chatkal district, revealing a widespread problem affecting access to legal assistance for citizens.

item.title: Rybakina Nominated for WTA Player of the Year Award
item.description: Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina is among five contenders for the WTA Player of the Year award. She won four tournaments in 2026, including two Grand Slams (Australian Open and US Open), defeating Aryna Sabalenka in both finals. Rybakina also topped the world rankings for the first time and won titles in Stuttgart and Ningbo.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Criticizes Officials for Poor Performance and Delays
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov stated that many local officials are failing to perform their duties, causing delays in resolving citizens' problems. He noted that people are forced to appeal to the head of state for issues that should be handled at regional levels. Japarov emphasized that increased salaries and expanded powers for officials necessitate concrete results.

item.title: Local Leaders Failing to Resolve Issues, Forcing Citizens to Appeal to President
item.description: Adylbek Kasymaliev, Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, expressed concern that issues within the purview of local authorities are reaching the President. He noted insufficient initiative in creating jobs and underutilization of allocated funds in some regions, contributing to internal migration and traffic congestion in Bishkek.

item.title: Turonbank Issues Statement Amidst Reports of Chairman's Arrest
item.description: Turonbank has released a statement addressing rumors circulating on social media and news outlets regarding the arrest of its chairman, Chori Mirzayev, on charges of embezzlement. The bank assures customers and partners that it continues to operate normally, with all services unaffected. They emphasize adherence to corporate governance and legal requirements.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Working to Reclaim State Property from Organized Crime and Corruption
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) is addressing efforts by some citizens to reclaim property transferred to the state as part of anti-corruption and anti-organized crime measures. GKNB Chairman Maksat Asanaliev stated that while state rights have been restored, some shortcomings in the process are being identified and rectified.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Orders Review of Law After Man Jailed for $2,000
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has called for a review of potential shortcomings in the law after a citizen reported their father was sentenced to two years imprisonment for a $2,000 sum. The president stated that while anti-corruption laws have been tightened, the situation lacks logic and humanity. He urged law enforcement, prosecution, and the judiciary to propose amendments.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Memorandum of Understanding for Parliamentary Cooperation with Saudi Arabia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Speaker of Parliament, Marlen Mamataliev, has proposed a memorandum of understanding for cooperation between the parliaments of Kyrgyzstan and Saudi Arabia. The proposal was discussed during a meeting with Abdullah bin Mohammed bin Ibrahim Al-Sheikh, Chairman of Saudi Arabia's Consultative Council. Mamataliev expressed interest in expanding bilateral ties, including inter-parliamentary engagement, trade, and investment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's President Criticizes Officials for Unresolved Regional Problems
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan has criticized heads of state and local authorities for failing to resolve long-standing issues in the regions. He noted that while progress is made in the capital, citizens' concerns in the regions remain unaddressed. Japarov stated that officials often blame each other, leading to unresolved conflicts. He announced that officials will be granted more authority to coordinate and resolve issues on-site.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Minister Highlights Shortcomings in Local Governance
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev acknowledged significant shortcomings in the local governance system during a national meeting on socio-economic development. He reported on progress in healthcare, education, and infrastructure, noting increased funding and construction of social facilities and roads. Tourism is also projected to grow.

item.title: Bishkek Thermal Power Plant Seeks Chemicals Worth 20 Million Som
item.description: The Bishkek Thermal Power Plant (TPP) is seeking to purchase 490 tons of construction lime and 74.8 tons of liquid bactericidal agent for its water treatment system. The total cost is estimated at 20.2 million som. These chemicals are crucial for preparing water for boilers and ensuring the efficient operation of the plant's equipment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Banks Report 1.81 Trillion Tenge Net Profit in First Nine Months of 2026
item.description: Kazakhstani banks earned a net profit of 1.81 trillion tenge in the first nine months of 2026, a decrease of approximately 238 billion tenge compared to the same period last year. The majority of profits came from large banks, accounting for about 90.7% of the total results for the top ten. Despite the profit decrease, bank assets and credit portfolios grew.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Prime Minister Outlines Development Priorities and Achievements
item.description: Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev presented Kyrgyzstan's social-economic development achievements, reform results, and strategic priorities. He highlighted significant increases in healthcare and education funding, with healthcare rising from 26 billion soms in 2021 to 73.1 billion in 2026, and education allocated 96 billion soms for 2026. Plans include building 262 social infrastructure facilities by 2026.

item.title: Appellate Court Reconsiders Release of Former Akym Karim Kokirekbaev Due to Illness
item.description: The criminal case court panel reviewed the legality of releasing former Akym Karim Kokirekbaev due to severe illness. The panel found gross violations of legal requirements by the Alatau city court, as the inmate's illness does not qualify for release. Consequently, the court's decision was overturned, and the request for release was denied. Separate rulings were issued regarding the prosecutor and penal system representative.

item.title: Taliban in Zabul Demand Sharia-Compliant Photos for Graduation Documents
item.description: Sources report that the Taliban in Zabul Province have mandated that students provide "Sharia-compliant" photographs to receive their Grade 12 graduation documents. The photos must depict students with beards, caps, and turbans. Non-compliant photos will result in the rejection of graduation documents.

item.title: Azerbaijan Deepens Ties with Central Asia Amid Shifting Geopolitics
item.description: Baku is actively engaging with Central Asia, becoming a full participant in regional leaders' consultative meetings and set to chair them in 2027. Azerbaijan has signed alliance treaties with Kyrgyzstan and an eternal friendship treaty with Uzbekistan, establishing joint investment funds. This growing cooperation occurs against a backdrop of disagreements between Baku and its ally Turkey.

item.title: Tajikistan Parliament Approves Investment Deals Linked to President's Relatives
item.description: Tajikistan's lower house of parliament approved the state budget for 2027 and five investment agreements. One agreement is with a company linked to Hasan Asadullozoda, the head of "Oryonbank" and the president's brother-in-law. Another involves the company "Faroz," reportedly linked to the president's son-in-law, Shamsullo Sohibov.

item.title: Kazakhstan MP Proposes Review of State Industrial Support Measures
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kazakhstan has proposed evaluating the effectiveness of state industrial support over the past five years. The goal is to reassess funding for inefficient measures and introduce new ones, considering added value, labor productivity, exports, and investment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks in Top 20 Digital Governments Globally by UN
item.description: Kazakhstan has climbed to 16th place in the UN's E-Government Development Index (EGDI), entering the top tier. The country improved its position by eight places in two years, surpassing Germany, Sweden, and Japan. Its EGDI score increased from 0.9009 in 2024 to 0.9363 in 2026.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Jordan Agree to Increase Air Traffic to 14 Flights Weekly
item.description: Kazakhstan and Jordan have agreed to expand their regular air service, signing a memorandum allowing up to 14 flights per week. The agreement was reached during the ICAO Air Transport Conference in Montreal. Royal Jordanian expressed interest in launching regular flights to Kazakhstan, noting growing tourism interest from Jordanian citizens.

item.title: Former Zhambyl Region Governor Sentenced to 12 Years, Later Released Due to Illness, Now Faces Appeal
item.description: Karim Kokrekbaev, former governor of Kazakhstan's Zhambyl Region, was sentenced to 12 years in prison in 2025. He was recently released due to severe illness. However, the prosecutor's office announced it is petitioning to overturn this release decision.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Processed Agricultural Exports Surge 35% to $3.4 Billion
item.description: Kazakhstan's processed agricultural exports reached $3.4 billion in the first nine months of 2026, a 35% increase year-on-year. Processed goods constituted over half of agricultural exports. The government aims to boost further exports through deep processing of grain into products like starch and bioethanol.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan SMEs Face Legal and Financial Barriers Despite $900 Million Growth Plan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan aims to attract up to $900 million for SMEs by 2030, but a government survey reveals over 80% of entrepreneurs lack confidence in legal protection. High interest rates, complex procedures, and worker shortages are also cited as obstacles. A consortium is coordinating support, with an action plan due in early 2027.

item.title: Tajikistan Officially Notifies UN of Withdrawal from International Criminal Court
item.description: Tajikistan has officially informed the UN of its withdrawal from the International Criminal Court (ICC). The withdrawal will take effect on November 20, 2027, one year after the notification. The country had signed the Rome Statute in 1998 and ratified it in 2000.

item.title: Russia Prepares Ferries Amid Fears of Transport Blockade for Kaliningrad
item.description: Russia is reportedly preparing ferries as a contingency measure in case of a transport blockade affecting the exclave of Kaliningrad. This move comes amid ongoing geopolitical tensions and concerns over supply routes.

item.title: Bangladesh Vows to Arrest Former PM Sheikh Hasina Upon Return from India
item.description: Bangladesh's government stated it will arrest and jail former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns from India, where she has been living since fleeing in 2024. Dhaka is seeking her extradition, citing an existing treaty, as Hasina faces a death sentence and her party is banned.

item.title: Kazakhstan Begins Clinical Trials for Locally Developed Orthopedic Implants
item.description: Surgeons in Kazakhstan have initiated clinical trials for domestically produced implants designed for spinal fusion and complex hip surgeries. These implants, developed by the Batpenov National Scientific Center and D. Serikbayev East Kazakhstan Technical University, utilize computer modeling and 3D printing. Trials are also underway for devices treating fractures and bone deformities, with a focus on safety and antibacterial properties.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Insurance Payout Guarantee Fund Joins IFIGS Leadership
item.description: For the first time in the history of its national insurance market, Uzbekistan's Insurance Payout Guarantee Fund has been elected to the leadership of the International Forum of Insurance Guarantee Schemes (IFIGS). The Fund's Director, Yormat Mirzaev, was chosen as First Vice-Chair. This appointment, effective from 2027, signifies Uzbekistan's successful integration into the global professional insurance community.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Assess Bank Transfers for Social Assistance Eligibility from 2027
item.description: Starting in 2027, Kazakhstan will change its approach to social assistance. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection announced that family income, assets, and financial obligations will be considered when assessing eligibility. The system will not access personal bank statements but will use aggregated, encrypted financial indicators from banks.

item.title: Spain Recognizes No Taliban Rule, Supports Criminalizing Gender Apartheid
item.description: Spain's Foreign Minister stated that his country does not recognize the Taliban and supports criminalizing gender apartheid. Speaking at a meeting of Afghan women activists, he emphasized that women's rights are non-negotiable and that Spain will work to include gender apartheid in the Convention on Crimes Against Humanity.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Proposes Dismissal of Some Mayors and Akims Amidst Criticism
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has criticized the performance of local authorities and proposed dismissing some mayors and akims. This follows a review of regional governance over nine months, which identified shortcomings in service delivery and cadre policy. Citizens have also complained about local officials' inaction on various issues.

item.title: Dangar District Irrigation System Construction Reaches 81% Completion
item.description: Construction of the 'Pushing' irrigation system in Tajikistan's Dangar district is 81% complete. The project, led by OJSC 'Tajikgidroelektromontazh', aims to improve agricultural infrastructure and water resource efficiency. Upon completion by mid-2027, it will provide modern drip irrigation to 530 hectares of farmland.

item.title: New Group of Wild Horses to Be Delivered to Kazakhstan from Europe
item.description: Preparations are underway to select and acclimatize wild horses for potential delivery to Kazakhstan in 2027. A 1.5-year-old male Przewalski's horse named Bruno was transported from Sweden to a special center in the Czech Republic. His eventual transfer to Kazakhstan is not yet confirmed.

item.title: Politician Ravshan Jeenbekov Accuses Top Officials from Prison
item.description: Imprisoned politician Ravshan Jeenbekov has filed a complaint against Prosecutor General Malik Bekturganov and GKNB Chairman Maksat Asanaliev. He demands prosecution of former Prosecutor General Kurmanul Zulueshev and others for alleged illegal detention and prosecution of 'Kempir-Abad defendants'.

item.title: New Cotton Processing Plant Launched in Karakalpakstan
item.description: A new cotton receiving and processing plant has been commissioned in Ellikkala district, Republic of Karakalpakstan. The plant, built by "Ellikkala oltin tolası cluster" LLC, has a capacity to process 30,000 tons of cotton annually and will create 110 new jobs.

item.title: Leaders of Financial Pyramid Branch Convicted in Zhetysu Region
item.description: A couple who led a financial pyramid branch under the CVK brand have been convicted in the Zhetysu region. They were found guilty of attracting funds from citizens with promises of high returns and have been sentenced to 2 years and 4 months of restricted freedom.

item.title: Global Environment Facility Resumes Small Grants Programme in Afghanistan
item.description: The Global Environment Facility (GEF) has restarted its Small Grants Programme in Afghanistan, offering opportunities for community-led environmental projects. Officials emphasized the need for international support to address climate change vulnerability.

item.title: Arrests of Samruk-Kazyna and KTZ Heads Do Not Affect Fitch Ratings
item.description: Fitch Ratings has stated that the recent arrests of the heads of 'Samruk-Kazyna' National Welfare Fund and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) national railway company have not impacted their credit ratings.

item.title: Almaty SuperSki Resort Construction Starts Amid Environmental Concerns Over Protected Trees
item.description: Construction has begun on the Almaty SuperSki mountain resort, with French company POMA pouring foundations for cable lifts. The project, developed by Kazakh Tourism Development, faces scrutiny over 472 protected trees in the path of a planned access road. The developer claims all trees are mapped and none fall within the construction footprint.

item.title: Bukhara School Roof Collapse Prompts Safety Concerns and Relocation of Students
item.description: A section of the roof at School No. 42 in Bukhara collapsed in October, leading authorities to deem the building unsafe for further use. Over 1,300 students have been temporarily relocated to two other schools. An inspection report from November 9 cited worn, rotten, and deformed roof structures, warning of potential collapse.
